## Context

Bug b636 (landed as 5e7d6e71ba) added deleted-source recovery to fsck. After the module-size split, `restore_deleted_sources` and `rebuild_with_restore` live in `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_restore.py` (:127 and :182) and are re-exported from `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` (bottom-of-module import at :614).

Only ONE call site actually uses the composed helper — `repair_or_plan` (`fsck_repair.py:580`). The per-ticket repair path `_repair_ticket` (`fsck_repair.py:209`) still calls `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` DIRECTLY at :270-274, so it rebuilds from whatever sources survive and never attempts the restore. That path fails closed rather than corrupting anything, but a ticket whose SNAPSHOT source was dropped by legacy compaction is not recovered when repair runs through `_repair_ticket`.

`rebuild_with_restore`'s own docstring already calls itself "the repair path's single entrypoint", and no ADR or ticket records an intentional divergence between the two paths — this is a residual gap, not a deliberate split.

Discovered while closing story 9f7f (superseded into b636): every other acceptance criterion of 9f7f is implemented, this call site is the residual gap.

## Plan

Route `_repair_ticket`'s rebuild through `rebuild_with_restore` so the two repair entry points behave identically, and surface any restored sources in the `disp` dict the caller already consumes.

### The `no_commit` contract (must be preserved)

`_repair_ticket` takes `no_commit: bool = False` and currently forwards it:
`rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir, no_commit=no_commit)`.
`no_commit` gates the git commit in `compact_rebuild.py:234`, and the batch repair loop at `fsck_repair.py:401-408` calls `_repair_ticket(..., no_commit=True)` so commits are deferred until after the whole batch.

`rebuild_with_restore(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]` has NO `no_commit` parameter and calls the rebuild with the default `no_commit=False`. Routing naively would make the batch path commit once per ticket — a behavior change.

Worked example of the required contract:

- `rebuild_with_restore` gains a keyword-only `no_commit: bool = False` and forwards it verbatim: `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir, no_commit=no_commit)`.
- `_repair_ticket` calls `rebuild_with_restore(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir, no_commit=no_commit)` and unpacks `(rebuilt, restored)`.
- The existing `repair_or_plan` call at `fsck_repair.py:580` stays `rebuild_with_restore(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir)` — the new parameter defaults to `False`, which is that path's current behavior, so it is unchanged.
- Concretely: `_repair_ticket(tracker, tid, dir, dry_run=False, no_commit=True)` on a ticket with an auto-recoverable orphan restores the deleted source, rebuilds the snapshot, and leaves the tickets worktree DIRTY (no new commit on the `tickets` branch); with `no_commit=False` it commits exactly as it does today.

### Reporting

`_repair_ticket`'s `disp` dict gains a `"restored"` key holding the restored filenames list (empty list when nothing was restored), mirroring what `repair_or_plan` surfaces as "after restoring N deleted event(s)".

### Import cycle

`fsck_repair` imports `fsck_restore` at the BOTTOM of the module (:614) to let the leaf lazily import `snapshot_missing_sources`. `_repair_ticket` therefore uses a function-local `from rebar._commands.fsck_restore import rebuild_with_restore` (the same lazy-import shape the current code uses for `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` at :270) rather than a new module-level import.

### No double-restore

`restore_deleted_sources` skips any name already present on disk as `<name>` or `<name>.retired`, and `rebuild_with_restore` only attempts a restore when `snapshot_missing_sources(ticket_dir)` is non-empty. A second pass over the same ticket therefore restores nothing and reports an empty list — that idempotency is the invariant AC4 asserts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_repair_ticket` obtains its rebuild through `rebuild_with_restore`, not a direct `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` call.
      Verify: `grep -n "rebuild_with_restore" src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` shows a call inside `_repair_ticket`, and `grep -n "rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log" src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` shows no call in `_repair_ticket`.
- [ ] `rebuild_with_restore` accepts a keyword-only `no_commit: bool = False` and forwards it to `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`; `_repair_ticket` passes its own `no_commit` through.
      Verify: `grep -n "no_commit" src/rebar/_commands/fsck_restore.py`.
- [ ] `_repair_ticket`'s returned `disp` dict carries a `"restored"` list of restored source filenames.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_repair_restore_08c8.py -q`.
- [ ] A held-out test proves a ticket whose SNAPSHOT source was deleted by legacy compaction is recovered when repair runs via `_repair_ticket` (RED before the change).
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_repair_restore_08c8.py -q`.
- [ ] A test proves `_repair_ticket(..., no_commit=True)` creates no new commit on the tickets branch while still restoring and rebuilding.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_repair_restore_08c8.py -q`.
- [ ] A test proves a second `_repair_ticket` pass over the same ticket restores nothing (no double-restore, empty `"restored"`).
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_repair_restore_08c8.py -q`.
- [ ] The `repair_or_plan` call site at `fsck_repair.py:580` is unchanged in behavior and existing fsck repair/restore tests pass unchanged.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/integration/test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py tests/interfaces/store -q -k "fsck or restore or repair"`.
